items.title: ADR: persisted user-derived embeddings or explicit prohibition
items.outcome: A reviewed decision either prohibits persisted user-derived embeddings or defines their store, tenancy, disclosure risk, retention and hard-delete erasure before any vector extension or embedding column can enter an environment.
items.context: The AI research names pgvector and transaction embeddings, while the accepted erasure design relies on crypto-shredding. A similarity-searchable vector cannot be application-layer encrypted and may leak source text through inversion, so silence would let an unowned datastore bypass the strongest privacy guarantees in the product.
scope: Separate static category prototypes and ephemeral inference from embeddings derived from a user's transaction, merchant, memo or assistant conversation
Decision on whether any user-derived embedding may be persisted on the server or device
Store, tenancy, row-level security and network boundary if persistence is approved
Embedding model, dimension, versioning and full re-index semantics
Retention, export and hard-delete erasure with a post-erasure residue query
Embedding-inversion and membership-inference threat analysis
Database extension allowlist consequence consumed by T-PLT-01
acceptance_criteria: The record chooses persisted or prohibited and rejects the alternative with a reason
Until the record is accepted, the database extension allowlist rejects pgvector and every user-derived embedding column
If persistence is approved, crypto-shredding is explicitly rejected as sufficient and a hard-delete residue test is specified
If persistence is approved, the model and vector dimension are pinned and a version change requires a complete re-index rather than mixed generations
If persistence is prohibited, static prototypes and ephemeral inference are bounded so no user-derived vector is written to durable storage
The record states whether conversation history and transaction enrichment may use the same store and rejects accidental cross-purpose reuse
The schema and policy consequences are published as machine-readable artifacts
contracts_schema: Decision artifact naming permitted embedding classes, stores, model versions, retention and erasure mechanism
security_privacy: Treats a user-derived embedding as personal financial data and an inversion-capable disclosure surface
No approved decision means no durable user-derived embedding
observability: If approved, requires vector counts by model version, stale-generation count, erasure residue result and cross-tenant denial rate
tests: Database extension allowlist rejection test while the ADR is open
Post-erasure similarity-query residue test if persistence is approved
Model-version re-index conformance test if persistence is approved
rollout_rollback: Decision only; any approved implementation remains default off until its erasure and tenancy tests pass
Rollback removes serving access and schedules verified hard deletion before removing the implementation
items.parallel_boundary: Primary repo docs. Owns one decision record and its machine-readable policy artifact; AI, API and infrastructure tickets consume the decision and do not redefine embedding policy.
definition_of_done: Document merged and dated, with the option chosen and rejected options recorded
Every acceptance criterion demonstrated by a named test or attached evidence
Machine-readable policy consumed by the database extension gate
Reviewed through a current-head core-reviewer attestation from a separate qualified reviewer-agent session

items.context: T-ING-03 owns server reconciliation, but no client owns the question, cash balance or correction flow. Without a journey, ATM withdrawals are either double-counted as spending or leave a cash account users cannot understand.

items.context: The base transaction contract covers creation and capture but not consumer refunds, cash adjustments or the lifecycle after recurring detection. These shapes affect balances, budgets and income, so private client conventions would create incompatible arithmetic.

items.context: The original promise included guidance about the salary needed to reach a goal. Current goal tickets calculate the gap but own no sourced labor-market information, leaving the promised next step absent or tempting an LLM to invent it.
